uncited: **Calculate Clip-Space AABB:** Compute the 2D bounding box of the triangle in clip space $(x, y)$, ignoring $z$.
**Compute Edge Planes:** For each edge of the triangle, calculate a homogeneous plane normal in 2D homogeneous space (using $x, y, w$ components).
**Expand Edge Planes:** Offset each plane normal's $z$ component (the constant term in the homogeneous line equation) outward.
**Compute New Vertices:** Calculate the intersection lines of the expanded planes.
The intersection line vector of two planes is the cross product of their normals.
**Fragment Shader Culling:** In the fragment shader, calculate the barycentric coordinates or distance to the original triangle edges.
- Precision issues may arise if the triangle is very small or very large in clip space.
- Degenerate triangles (zero area) may produce undefined plane normals.
- **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of triangles, as each triangle is processed in the geometry shader.
- **Memory Complexity:** Low, as it only stores temporary plane data in the geometry shader.
Performance may be impacted by the complexity of the plane intersection calculations.
- **When to use:** When using standard rasterization pipelines and encountering voxelization holes, especially in multi-view projection scenarios.
It is part of a broader effort to improve the quality of rasterization-based voxelization techniques.
